source: AHN5, Dutch national airborne laser scan (Kadaster, open data via PDOK), sub-tiles 25GN1_01 and 25EZ1_21
encoding: interleaved int16 x, int16 y (scene units /32767), uint8 z, uint8 cat (low nibble: 0 ground cell, 1 canopy, 2 roof cell, 15 void; high nibble: hillshade 0..15 for ground); 6 bytes/point
assumptions: ground = median z of classification 2 per 1.5 m cell

canopy = highest classification-1 return per 1 m cell, at least 2 m above the local ground median, then a 3 x 3 mean over occupied cells; AHN does not label vegetation, so this is height above ground, not a species or leaf attribute
building = 90th percentile of classification-6 returns per 1.2 m cell
water gives the laser no return, so the canal is the gap in the ground; bridges (26) excluded
0 returns above 45 m NAP dropped (a single spire), so the houses keep their proportions

ground and roof cells ship as full grids with empty cells marked void and are drawn as surfaces (11 one-cell ground holes with 6+ occupied neighbours filled with their median); canopy tops are thinned uniformly to the point budget; no derived quantity computed
canopy noise filter: a canopy cell keeps only with at least 5 of 8 occupied neighbours, in a patch of at least 12 cells, and not within 2 cells of a roof at or above its height (1053 cells dropped)
